title_original: Jimmy Jenkins’s ‘God With Us,’ Starring Rotimi & Lil Rel Howery, Lands PVOD Release

blocks.text: EXCLUSIVE: God With Us , the latest feature from independent filmmaker Jimmy Jenkins , will be available to rent and purchase on PVOD platforms from December 1.

The film, a modern American twist on the nativity story, lands on PVOD platforms after a booming performance on a limited theatrical release via Variance Films in partnership with Blue Harbor Entertainment. The film took a sizable $885k on 432 screens over its opening weekend. Those dollars came largely without planned Saturday or Sunday evening showtimes, although theaters were adding them throughout the weekend. Originally programmed as a one-weekend engagement, God With Us will remain in theaters throughout the holiday season. It has now passed $1.1 million.

blocks.text: Written and directed by Jenkins, the film follows inner-city childhood sweethearts Mary Anne Thomas and Joseph “Junie” Love as they embark on a divine mission from God: to lead a universal rebellion and give birth to the Savior of the world.

The film’s ensemble cast features Aspen Kennedy ( The Forge ) and Ashley Olivia Fisher ( Average Joe ), Rotimi ( Coming to America ), Roger Guenveur Smith ( Do the Right Thing ), Ashley Rios ( Cross ), Gregory Alan Williams ( Remember the Titans ), Clifton Powell ( Ray ), and Lil Rel Howery ( Get Out ).
God With Us is Jenkins’s sophomore feature following Sinners Wanted . He also co-directed the Showtime doc Basketball County: In the Water alongside John Beckham.

“When this film went out to buyers, the answer was basically, ‘Who’s going to show up for this?’ So we stopped asking and went straight to the people who’d been with me for ten years, from the stage plays to Basketball County ,” Jenkins said in a statement.

“Ten million trailer views sent us to theaters. The audience kept us there. Theaters held us over in Atlanta, Baltimore, Chicago, Detroit, Dallas, and across the DMV, and those were bookings we didn’t have to beg for.”
Jenkins added: “This audience has always been there: Black, faith-driven, family-centered, and ready to spend. The industry just hasn’t treated them like a market. We did.”
